feesApplyText:
Any offer accepted will be subject to contract, satisfactory referencing, and Right to Rent checks. At the start of the tenancy, you will be required to pay the rent and deposit due under the Tenancy Agreement.


Referencing and Right to Rent checks

Before referencing can begin, you will be required to complete an application form. You must also provide original photographic identification (such as a passport, national ID card, visa, residence permit, or driving licence) together with proof of address (for example, an original utility bill, council tax bill, or bank statement dated within the last three months). If a guarantor is required, they will need to complete an application form and provide photographic identification along with proof of address.

Referencing will include checks against credit files and public records, anti-money laundering checks, confirmation of employment and income, verification of previous tenancy details, and Right to Rent checks. Upon receipt of a satisfactory referencing a tenancy start date will be confirmed.

Tenant deposit

In England, under the Tenant Fees Act 2019, tenancy deposits for new and renewed tenancies are capped at the equivalent of five weeks rent (or six weeks rent where the annual rent is £50,000 or more). This is calculated by dividing the annual rent by 52 and multiplying by five (or six where applicable). The deposit is payable at the start of the tenancy and is subject to satisfactory referencing.

Holding deposit

In England, the Tenant Fees Act 2019 limits holding deposits to the equivalent of one week s rent. A holding deposit is paid to reserve a property and is calculated by multiplying the monthly rent by 12 to determine the annual rent, then dividing by 52. The holding deposit will be payable once your offer has been accepted. Full details of the circumstances under which the holding deposit will be refunded or retained are set out on the application form.

Tenant Fees Act 2019 permits certain fees / charges to be made under the following circumstances:

Fee£ Inc. VAT Explanation

Default Fee for Late Payment of rent

Interest shall be charged on rent overdue by more than 14 days, calculated daily at a rate of 3% above the Bank of England base rate until payment is made in full.

Loss of a key or any other security device.

Landlords and letting agents may charge a tenant a fee to cover the cost of replacing a lost key or security device (such as a fob or electronic device for garage doors or security gates).

Payment in respect of a variation, assignment, or novation of a tenancy.£50.00 +VATAt the tenant s request, a landlord or letting agent may charge a fee for the variation, assignment, or replacement of a tenancy. The fee is £50 (including VAT).

Should you require further clarification, please ask us to explain these to you.

We are members of:

The Property Ombudsman Redress Scheme N00993

Safe Agent Client Money Protection Scheme A3474

Please note that lettings agents are required by law to publish on their website s information for potential tenants about relevant fees, redress schemes and client money protection schemes (including the names of those schemes). Relevant fees must also be published on third party websites, such as Rightmove. For properties to rent in England and Wales, details of the agent's membership of any redress scheme and client money protection scheme must also be published with their fees on Rightmove. It is the agent's responsibility to ensure that all relevant information is provided to Rightmove and is up to date and accurate. If the relevant information does not appear here, the agent may have included it within the property description.
